key_insight: UniTB combines tight-binding physical priors with equivariant deep learning to predict electronic Hamiltonians across diverse chemistries while constraining unphysical band shifts.
engineering_relevance: Its fast UniTB-Flash variant supports large-cell calculations and materials screening with linear-cost prior assembly, while UniTB provides more accurate property predictions.
method: Learn E(3)-equivariant corrections to a physically motivated prior Hamiltonian.
Use prior-routed mixture-of-experts learning and a charge-equilibration head to generalize across chemistry.
Bound band shifts through projection; accelerate computation with SO(2) GPU kernels and two-center tables in UniTB-Flash.
evidence_signal: Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB achieved 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements; both variants matched DFT optical and conductivity results for amorphous Ge-Sb-Te without amorphous training data.
watch_item: Reported accuracy is for nonmagnetic test crystals, so performance on magnetic materials and broader disordered chemistries remains to be established.
paper_title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
